Mediastinal germ-cell tumor; the mediastinum itself has no axis, and no origin or common invasion of a covered organ is specified.

Macular degeneration, callosal malformation and intellectual disability define the syndrome.
Inborn neurotransmitter synthesis disorder causing severe progressive infantile encephalopathy; treatment-induced dyskinesias add no axis.
Inherited dystrophies affecting the superficial corneal layers.

Microlissencephaly with severe developmental impairment; cardiac and retinal abnormalities are occasional (5-29%); vascular ancestry is unsupported by the phenotype.

Usually a gonadal germ-cell tumor; adult designation does not establish a tumor origin in any covered organ.
Inherited deficiency of a coagulation inhibitor; thrombosis is a separately diagnosed consequence rather than established common direct vascular damage.
Mesenchymal soft-tissue malignancy in the solitary fibrous tumor spectrum; no specific visceral or CNS origin is given.
Reproductive-associated syndrome with self-limited systemic symptoms; no established organ damage or proven immune mechanism.
Neurodevelopmental disease with defining visual dysfunction; strabismus/nystagmus in 3/5. Septal cardiac defects occur in 2/5 (40%); infections alone do not prove immunodeficiency.
Immune-cell deficiency; hearing loss 80-99%, optic nerve abnormalities/visual loss 30-79%. Secondary infections/respiratory failure and later leukemia excluded.
Melanoma arising in scrotal skin; reproductive location does not remove its cutaneous origin.
Benign nerve-sheath neoplasm arising in gallbladder nerves; the definition overrides inconsistent malignant and CNS ancestry.
Congenital kidney and urinary tract malformations, including ureteropelvic junction obstruction.
Direct infection and inflammation of joints.
SNCA-associated neurodegeneration causing parkinsonism, dementia and autonomic dysfunction; orthostatic hypotension does not establish separate vascular injury.
Congenital split spinal cord; associated vertebral deformities and scoliosis occur in roughly half of patients and constitute structural skeletal involvement.
Skeletal dysplasia with platyspondyly, abnormal vertebral endplates and disproportionate short-trunk stature.
